description: A four-panel composite figure that pairs SEM micrographs with EPMA Nb elemental maps for two as-cast medium-Mn low-density steels, combining microstructure morphology with chemical-composition analysis. (a) is an SEM micrograph annotated "as-cast 0.02Nb" with a 20 µm scale bar; it shows equiaxed polygonal austenite grains carrying a sparse population of irregular, vermicular/flower-shaped dark second-phase particles that bear bright (high-contrast) rims. (b) is the corresponding Nb EPMA map of the same field: an almost uniformly dark-blue background interrupted by a single isolated bright cyan Nb-enriched spot near the centre. (c) is an SEM micrograph annotated "as-cast 0.04Nb" with a 20 µm scale bar, showing the same polygonal grain structure but with more numerous and larger irregular second-phase particles. (d) is its Nb map, again mostly dark blue but with several bright cyan Nb-rich patches aligned with the second-phase features, clearly more numerous than in (b). No composition colour scale, intensity legend or numeric count is printed on either map. Together the panels demonstrate that Nb is essentially uniformly dissolved in the austenite matrix of both steels, with only sporadic, locally enriched Nb at the boundaries of the coarse second-phase features, and that enrichment is more frequent in the 0.04Nb steel.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an SEM micrograph labelled 'as-cast 0.02Nb' with a 20 µm scale bar showing polygonal austenite grains plus sparse irregular vermicular dark particles with bright rims.
Panel (c) is an SEM micrograph labelled 'as-cast 0.04Nb' with a 20 µm scale bar showing the same polygonal grain structure with more numerous and larger irregular second-phase particles than in (a).
Panel (b) is a Nb EPMA map dominated by a uniform dark-blue field with a single isolated bright cyan Nb-enriched spot near the centre, indicating uniform Nb dispersion with sporadic enrichment.
Panel (d) is a Nb EPMA map with several bright cyan Nb-enriched patches aligned with the irregular second-phase features, visibly more abundant than in panel (b).
Neither Nb map (b) or (d) carries a printed colour scale bar, intensity legend or numeric composition value.
The caption identifies panels (a,b) as the as-cast 0.02Nb steel and panels (c,d) as the 0.04Nb steel, analysed by EPMA.
The citing text states that Nb is uniformly dispersed within the austenite grain, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries in the Nb-containing steels.

The citing text states that the slight variations in ferrite and NbC content have minimal impact on the chemical composition of austenite in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, particularly for Al and C, the crucial κ-carbide constituents.
The citing text links this figure with Figure 6 to infer that Nb atoms are present within the κ-carbides.
